raw_response:
I will keep it simple and do what I trust most here in Quzhou County: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on the same land. That is the system I know, it fits our local weather and irrigation conditions, and at my age I would rather choose a steady, familiar pattern than take risks on crops that need more labor or more careful market timing. I will use improved seed, not expensive high-risk choices, and I will manage fertilizer and water in a moderate way so I can protect yield without overspending. For wheat, I will focus on a solid base fertilizer, a few irrigations at key stages, and a small number of pesticide sprays only when needed for aphids, rust, or weeds. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, keep tillage light with rotary tillage to save labor, give enough nitrogen for grain filling, irrigate only a couple of times if rainfall is short, and control weeds and borers with limited sprays. My goal is stable production, manageable labor, and dependable grain from the same fields through the whole year.
